root_cause: The drawer opens via show()/showModal() but focus is not programmatically moved into the dialog, leaving keyboard users unable to reach the close button or form controls without a pointer.
repair_strategy: In DialogBase._showElement, after showing the dialog, queue a microtask to focus the first focusable element within the dialog, ensuring keyboard focus lands on the close button immediately when the drawer opens.
expected_accessibility_effect: When the drawer opens via keyboard (Enter on Filters button), focus immediately moves to the close button (#filters-close), allowing sequential Tab navigation through all form controls (#in-stock, #waterproof, #apply) without a pointer.
functional_risks: If a dialog intentionally manages focus differently (e.g., expects focus on a specific element via autofocus), this could override that intention.
The focusable selector might not match all focusable element types (e.g., custom elements with tabindex, area, iframe).
If the dialog content is dynamically loaded, the first focusable element might not exist yet when the microtask runs.
verification_requirements: After pressing Enter on #filters-open, focus must be on #filters-close.
Subsequent Tab presses must move focus to #in-stock, then #waterproof, then #apply.
Escape key must close the drawer and return focus to #filters-open.
Clicking Show results must update the applied output correctly.
Ensure the drawer still opens/closes correctly for mouse users.
Modal dialogs (showModal) should continue to work with browser auto-focus.
